dialogues.speaker: Remnant Records: I
dialogues.text: Wow, how surprising, that something assembled with spare parts could actually be so powerful.

dialogues.speaker: Remnant Records: I
dialogues.text: We'll deal with it according to our orders from above.

dialogues.speaker: Remnant Records: I
dialogues.text: After it is cleaned up, we'll throw it in the shallows.

dialogues.speaker: Remnant Records: I
dialogues.text: Once buried in the sea sand, its energy should quickly drain out.

dialogues.speaker: Remnant Records: I
dialogues.text: The device will probably still affect nearby areas... but it should stop working after a while and make no further trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Many records are lost, and these pages are all that remain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D'you think these notes were left by the Fatui?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "We'll deal with it according to our orders from above." Could this be a destruction guide for the device assembled with spare parts?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The destruction process is just to "leave it in the shallows" ...Paimon thinks it means to bury it by the seashore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But didn't the Fatui make these devices in the first place? Why destroy them?

choices.text: Maybe there's some conflict between factions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Inside the Fatui? That's hard to imagine...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But the mechanism wasn't mentioned in the notes at all. What on earth is that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't we have a look around? There might be other records nearby!

choices.text: Maybe it's because of some personal beef.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is... is that so? Paimon guesses the Fatui are actually quite complicated...
